transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because I just keep getting these awful doubts that I've missed something important. 

It happens with all sorts of things. I'll worry that I messed up a number on the mortgage payment, or missed a clause in a client proof at work, or even just left the front door unlatched. And the frustrating part is, even when I know I already checked it, the thought just barges right back into my head. It always comes down to this intense feeling of, well, what if this is the mistake that costs you everything? It's just getting really exhausting to deal with.
When these thoughts occur, do you feel an internal pressure or a need to perform specific actions—like checking, counting, or repeating things—to try and make the anxiety go away?

Yes, I definitely do. It's exactly like a pressure. I end up reopening files I've already saved and closed, or I'll reread emails over and over. If it's a bill, I'll keep checking the online payment confirmation just to be sure. 

And sometimes I'll just keep saying the figures silently in my head until they finally feel... I don't know, settled, I guess. It's really impacting my work, honestly, because doing all that can turn a simple invoice or a basic logo revision into hours of extra time that I just can't bill for.
